answer: An agent market requires a refundable bond for each active job, whether selling a lagoon map or a quill illustration. A cipher links each escrow receipt to its contract, and payment waits for a verifiable delivery check. Creating more identities grants no extra capacity: every simultaneous job still needs its own bond. An attacker must lock capital across all fake agents, forgo its use elsewhere, and lose the posted bond when a delivery provably fails the agreed check.
